citeAs: To cite your use of the Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB), a joint project of UC San Diego and Broad Institute, please reference Subramanian, Tamayo, et al. (2005, PNAS) and one or more of the following as appropriate: Liberzon, et al. (2011, Bioinformatics), Liberzon, et al. (2015, Cell Systems), and also the source for the gene set as listed on the gene set page.  If you use Mouse MSigDB, please also cite Castanza, et al. (2023, Nature Methods).
conditionsOfAccess: Please register to download the GSEA software and the MSigDB gene sets, and to use our web tools. After registering, you can log in at any time using your email address. Registration is free. Its only purpose is to help us track usage for reports to our funding agencies.
dct:provenance: Authoritative discovery began at the configured MSigDB homepage and traversed the Human and Mouse collection pages, current-release documentation, license pages, and the official data.broadinstitute.org release listings. The complete public file listings for current Human release 2026.1.Hs and Mouse release 2026.1.Mm were downloaded, together with the machine-readable release catalog. Historical release directories were discovered but intentionally excluded because this artifact describes the current release; community-contributed gene sets explicitly described as not part of MSigDB, GSEA software, HTML pages, images, and unrelated site assets were excluded. The website's Downloads endpoint redirects anonymous users to registration, while the same files listed by the authoritative collection pages were publicly readable from the official Broad data host without credentials. All 10 ZIP archives were inspected without modifying them; every one of their 274 non-directory members is represented with its exact archive-relative contentUrl and containedIn reference. GMT files contain no in-band header. Their three logical labels (geneSetName, description, geneIdentifiers) were derived from the authoritative GSEA GMT format documentation; only the first five rows were reviewed and the variable-width member columns are represented as an array beginning at the documented third logical column. CHIP headers were preserved exactly. XML is represented as raw lines because Croissant 1.1 provides no XPath extractor. JSON member names were derived from at most five records. SQLite columns and declared types were read from PRAGMA table_info without sampling row values. The top-level Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license applies generally, but the source license page states that some gene sets have further restrictions: KEGG MEDICUS sets use CC BY-SA 4.0, KEGG_LEGACY sets are subject to Kanehisa Laboratories policies, and BioCarta-derived sets are subject to the linked disclaimer. Users must consult the source license page and per-gene-set license metadata. The conditionsOfAccess quotation reflects the official registration policy even though the enumerated official data-host URLs returned HTTP 200 anonymously. No sampled source schema contained coherent latitude/longitude or country-region-locality columns, so no GeoCoordinates hierarchy is supported.
description: The Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB) is a resource of tens of thousands of annotated gene sets for use with GSEA software, divided into Human and Mouse collections.
